Landing.headline: Only the jobs <jump>How it works</jump> that can actually hire you.
Landing.subline: Pemby checks who can legally pay you where you live, then sends only those roles. You apply yourself.

drop.caption: PDF or DOCX, up to 5 MB. No account needed. Deleted after 24 hours unless you sign up.

how.title: Drop a CV once. Pemby does the watching.
how.intro: No feed to scroll and no searches to save. You tell Pemby who you are, and it tells you when a job that can hire you appears.

drop.title: Drop your CV
drop.body: Pemby reads it and fills in your profile. No account needed. A CV nobody claims is deleted after 24 hours.

confirm.title: Confirm a few cards
confirm.body: Three short steps, already filled in from your CV: where you can work from, how you want to work, and the role and money.

deliver.title: Hear when a match appears
deliver.body: Only jobs that pass every check, one message per job, on Telegram, by email or as a web push. Quiet hours are yours to set.
deliver.label: New match
deliver.reason3: Go and Postgres, like your last role

apply.title: Apply yourself, with a kit
apply.body: Drafts of a cover letter, CV bullets for this job and screening answers, based on your own CV. You read, edit and send them.

trust.title: Every match shows why it can hire you.
trust.intro: A “remote” label says nothing about your country. Pemby reads what the company actually says, per country and per way of working, and shows you the reason with the verdict.
trust.tableCaption: Kestrel Systems, Senior Backend Engineer, for someone in Moldova

b2b.reason: “We work with contractors in Moldova, Georgia and Armenia.”

eor.reason: Hires through an EOR provider. Moldova is not named.

visa.reason: The post does not mention relocation.

local.reason: Payroll entities in Germany and Poland only.

yellow.name: Yellow
yellow.who: Sent to anyone who opts in

trust.liveTitle: Checked again on the company’s own careers page.
trust.liveBody: Every open job is re-read at the source at least every 12 hours. When a job is gone, Pemby closes it and pulls it from your Brief, so you don’t spend an evening on a posting that no longer exists.

silence.title: Some days the honest answer is nothing.
silence.body: A feed would fill this space with something. Pemby tells you nothing passed today, groups the near misses by what blocked them, and lets you loosen one thing with a tap.
silence.cardSummary: 6 near misses, grouped by what blocked them
silence.fixNote: Fixes are buttons in the product. Here they only show what you would see.

passes.title: Free to start. Pay once if you want it sooner.

items.one: Every match the moment it appears

passes.terms: One-time payment. No subscription, no auto-renew. Renewing adds to the time you have left, and an active pass with no match for 14 days gets 14 days added.

about.title: Built by an engineer who was underpaid by middlemen.
about.body1: Stephen Golban is a Moldovan software engineer with 7 years of experience. He was underpaid by middlemen.
about.body2: Pemby watches companies’ own careers pages for jobs that can hire you where you live. You apply yourself.
about.operator: Pemby is operated by his company, <link>Syncra Studio</link>.
about.code: The code is public, under AGPL-3.0, <link>on GitHub</link>.

telegram.title: Not ready to drop a CV? See example matches.
telegram.body: The public Pemby channel posts example green matches 24 hours after they appear, so you can see what Pemby finds. No account, no CV.

close.title: See what can actually hire you.
close.last: And if nothing can today, Pemby will say so.
